newsitem.title: LEBANON: Byblos Bank to raise capital to $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: Byblos Bank to raise capital to $200 mln.

text.p: Lebanon's Byblos Bank announced on Thursday that it will increase its capital to $200 million in the next 18 months.
Chairman Francois Bassil said the bank had "the intention to capitalise our bank at $200 million during the coming 18 months."
The increase will make Byblos one of the most heavily capitalised banks in Lebanon.

According to the bank's audited 1996 results issued earlier this month, capital was increased last year to $105 million from $73 million. The bank's profits rose 60 percent in 1996 to $24 million while total assets rose 38 percent to $1.43 billion.
Bassil said Byblos Bank shares would start trading on the Beirut Stock Exchange in May.

Byblos is considered one of Lebanon's most dynamic banks. According to the Almanac of the Lebanese Banks Association, it has 27 branches in Lebanon and an offshore branch in Cyprus. It has 579 employees.
